Inutos din niya ang pag-iisyu ng prangkisa sa mga public utility vehicle kung saan maraming pasahero.

I’ve been fortunate to have built businesses around the globe but this has occasionally exposed me to undesirable behaviour by people hired to help run these business and at other companies in the same sectors.

Maybe 15 years or so ago, the company that licensed the Bodog brand for Asian markets underwent a senior management shakeup. Unfortunately, the new guy they installed at the top developed a serious case of what I call ‘Manila Rock Star Syndrome.’

This malady isn’t Manila-specific; it applies to any Westerner earning a high salary in a region where the average wage is Western poverty level. Coupled with company-supplied condo/car/etc., some guys come to believe that they’re ‘special’ or ‘better’ and are just owed this.

Worse, these individuals can carry this attitude into the office, viewing the locally hired staff as beneath their stature and treating them accordingly. This is obviously toxic to the workplace, as no one wants to bust their ass for someone who looks down on them.

The Asian licensee was based in Manila, where I had a place and was spending a lot of time. As a recognizable figure in the gaming sector, the company’s owners hoped a quiet word from me might help nudge their ‘rock star’ back onto the right path.

So I met the guy, told him I’d seen ex-pats in Saint Kitts, Costa Rica and elsewhere go down this route and it didn’t end well. The people who worked for him deserved his respect, and I reminded him that he signs the back of his paycheck; the guys who hired him sign the front.

But as the saying goes, some men you just can’t reach. He knew I wasn’t involved in the day-to-day anymore and had no power to turf him myself, so he told me to get lost. He lasted a few more months before the bridges he’d lit on fire collapsed under the weight of his own ego.

I saw the guy here and there over the next few years at gaming conferences, drink in hand, talking loud and saying nothing. He bounced from company to company for a while but ultimately became unemployable as he kept repeating the same old mistakes.

I still encounter this ‘syndrome’ at some of my own businesses around the globe now and then. These guys (and the odd girl) get one warning. After that, they can go sing karaoke at some dive bar and live out their rock star fantasies on their own time.
